note.note:
Subjective:
- Presenting complaint/reason for visit:
  - Acute difficulty breathing and concern for allergic reaction after an insect sting (bee/wasp) a few minutes prior to consultation.
  - Localized rash at sting site on right arm; puncture mark present.
  - Patient reports possible mild swelling of right side of lip and "weird" sensation of tongue.
  - Patient feels anxious about possible progression of symptoms.
- History of present illness:
  - Onset: a few minutes prior to teleconsult.
  - Progression: symptoms present since sting; patient reports not acutely worse at time of call.
  - No antihistamines or other medication taken yet.
- Past medical history:
  - Eczema.
- Previous surgeries:
  - Not documented.
- Medications:
  - None documented. (Patient stated he has not taken any medication for this episode.)
- Social history:
  - Works as a computer scientist.
  - Lives alone.
  - Has a cat at home.
  - Occasional anxiety/panic attacks; no prior medication for anxiety.
- Allergies:
  - Penicillin.

Objective:
- General/airway/breathing:
  - Patient speaking coherently; breathing observed by clinician to be adequate at time of video assessment.
  - No stridor or audible airway compromise reported or observed.
- Head/neck/oral cavity:
  - Oral/throat exam via patient device: clinician had visualized mouth/throat; no swelling of oral soft tissues noted.
  - Clinician noted lips do not appear swollen on inspection.
- Skin/limb:
  - Right arm: puncture mark with slight redness and blotchy rash at sting site; clinician did not observe significant surrounding swelling or warmth at time of exam.
- Investigations:
  - None performed or ordered during this encounter.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Insect sting (bee/wasp sting):
   - Assessment: Localized allergic reaction to insect sting.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Anaphylaxis/systemic allergic reaction (risk considered but not present at time of examination).
     - Localized inflammatory reaction.
   - Investigations planned:
     - None planned at this time.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Recommend over-the-counter oral antihistamine: chlorphenamine (Piriton) 4 mg tablet — one tablet, up to every 4–6 hours as needed, up to six times daily (as discussed). Alternatively, a once-daily non-sedating antihistamine may be used per patient preference.
     - Monitor for spreading redness, increasing warmth, or signs of local infection (may require antibiotic if infection develops).
     - Provide patient education about signs of airway compromise and anaphylaxis.
   - Relevant referrals/urgent actions:
     - Advise immediate presentation to Emergency Department (A&E) if breathing worsens, lip/tongue swelling increases, stridor develops, or other signs of anaphylaxis occur.
     - Return to primary care or contact clinician if symptoms persist or worsen.

2. Anxiety about allergic reaction:
   - Assessment: Situational anxiety related to insect sting and possible allergic reaction.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - Panic attack (if acute worsening of anxiety-related symptoms).
   - Investigations planned:
     - None.
   - Treatment planned:
     - Reassurance, information provided about anaphylaxis signs.
     - Advise low threshold to contact clinician for support or reassessment if worried.
   - Relevant referrals:
     - None initiated during this visit.

3. Eczema (history):
   - Assessment: History of eczema.
   - Differential diagnosis:
     - N/A for this encounter.
   - Investigations planned:
     - None.
   - Treatment planned:
     - No treatment changes discussed during this encounter.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements:
  - Vital signs (respiratory rate, heart rate, blood pressure, oxygen saturation, temperature) were not recorded.
  - Current chronic medication list and past surgical history not documented.
  - Exact antihistamine dosing/brand alternatives were discussed verbally; prescription details not documented (medication available OTC).
- Internal conflicts from the transcript:
  - Patient reports swelling of right side of lip; clinician reports lips do not appear swollen on inspection — conflict noted.
- Transcript quality:
  - Audio/visual interaction sufficient for assessment; clinician was able to visualize mouth and sting site. No significant inaudible portions affecting clinical content.
